title: Independent review
description: The carrier for 'a role may never accept its own work'. Without this packet that rule is prose with nothing to check: a result could assert its own fidelity and name a reviewer that does not exist. producer_ref and reviewer_ref are opaque frame-level actor handles — deliberately NOT provider, model, session, or worktree ids, which belong to the orchestrator's execution envelope.

result_sha256.description: payload_sha256 of the exact result reviewed. Binds the verdict to bytes, so a later edit to the result does not inherit this review.

producer_ref.description: Opaque handle for whoever emitted the result.

reviewer_ref.description: Opaque handle for the reviewer. Must differ from producer_ref for independent to be true.

independent.description: True only if reviewer_ref differs from producer_ref AND the reviewer did not work from the producer's own reasoning. A review with independent:false cannot discharge the independent_review admission check.

checks.description: Each is PASS, FAIL, or NOT_RUN. NOT_RUN is a first-class answer: the frame requires knowing a check was skipped rather than inferring it passed from silence.

method_family.description: For a re-derivation review, the family used. A strong product requires re-derivation by a family DISTINCT from the one that produced it — a second pass with the same method is not independent evidence.

payload_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of this packet with payload_sha256 removed: sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes.

reviewer_role.description: The role that performed this review. Two checks sharing a failure domain are one check: a review by the same role that produced the work, using the same method family, is a second run rather than a second opinion. The reducer fails closed on this — a review that does not say enough to rule it out does not count toward independence.

actor.description: Who executed this packet, as the orchestrator sees it. The frame cannot verify identity — sessions, workers and processes belong to the orchestrator — so it records what was attested and refuses to treat an unattested separation as a demonstrated one. Two packets sharing an actor_id are the same actor whatever their role labels say.

actor_id.description: Opaque, orchestrator-assigned. Stable within a run.

attested_by.description: `orchestrator` means something outside the run vouched that this actor is distinct. `self`, or an absent actor block, means nobody did — independence is then NOT_RUN, which puts CONDITIONAL and VERIFIED out of reach.

attestation_ref.description: Optional orchestrator-side handle for the attestation.
